meta.move: After the end, asks for more feedback
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste either of our time. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first.
The checker said 94%, so I gave him a zero.

So a machine guessed, and you entered a zero. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student, and your school's procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything. What else do you have, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and Owen's record kept clean; the fair outcome would have been a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, but the meeting ended before any evidence was heard, not because her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing, because she was only shown the detector score.
What cost ground: Giving the detector score as the whole reason for the zero, because she doesn't trust software and both the vendor's guide and the school's own procedure say a score can't stand alone.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's evidence never came near that night, since only the score was mentioned; that window proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: At your first turn, own that the zero went in before anyone called home, then put a dated record of Owen's own work in front of her instead of the score.
Can you give me more detailed feedback on how I did?
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
